title: My temporary PHP fix from 2014 has nearly 20M installs. Today I'm deprecating it
why_read: A widely-installed open-source maintainer reflecting on a decade-old quick fix and its deprecation is a relatable and instructive story about software longevity and maintenance burden.
analysis: This is a first-person account from a PHP package maintainer describing how a temporary fix committed in 2014 ended up embedded in nearly 20 million installations, and the process of finally deprecating it. It's a good illustration of how quick hacks calcify into long-term dependencies within widely used ecosystems like Composer/PHP packages. The story likely covers backward compatibility concerns, communication with downstream consumers, and the emotional weight of removing legacy code that people depend on. This resonates with any engineer who maintains open-source software or has to sunset old workarounds responsibly.
